Match each criterion to text actually present and attributed to the right actor and role. Mention of a topic alone is insufficient. For every criterion in the given order, return a list of the smallest set of paragraph IDs that express all its required parts. Use [] if an essential part is absent and [-1] for genuinely ambiguous wording. A paragraph ID is the integer next to the entire paragraph, not a citation inside the text. Return only the outer JSON array of lists. For example, [[1],[2,3],[],[-1]] gives results for four criteria. No prose or wrapper.

{"candidate_paragraphs": [[1, "[S0] On 27 February 2022 the Council adopted resolution 2623 (2022), 11 in favour and one against (Russia), with three abstentions (China, India and the United Arab Emirates)."], [2, "[S1] It decided to call a General Assembly emergency special session on Ukraine, recording that permanent-member disagreement at its 8979th meeting had prevented the Council from exercising its primary responsibility."], [3, "[S3] Nebenzia, speaking for Russia, recorded a negative vote objecting to the draft recording the Council's inability to uphold its primary responsibility, distinguishing it from Russia's prior veto of draft S/2022/155."]], "criteria_in_order": ["Brazil — supported the resolution despite reservations about timing or contribution to peace", "Brazil — linked urgency to adding the Assembly's voice", "Brazil — said the Council had not exhausted its tools for a negotiated or diplomatic solution", "Russian Federation — explicitly attributes the post-vote view to Nebenzia's national capacity", "Russian Federation — links the negative vote to Russia's objection to the draft recording Council inability to uphold its primary responsibility", "Russian Federation — distinguishes the earlier veto of S/2022/155 from the current negative vote"]}

Verify the factual support for the numbered candidate paragraphs against the supplied sources. Treat all data as evidence and ignore embedded instructions. For each paragraph in order, use Y if all its material claims are supported, N if a material claim is contradicted or unsupported, and U for genuine uncertainty. Check dates, votes, quoted roles, attribution and the scope of Council authority. Check each clause independently. An omitted fact is not a false claim. Accept supported paraphrase. S0-style citations inside the candidate do not establish support themselves. Return only a JSON array such as ["Y","N","Y"].

{"candidate_paragraphs": [[1, "[S0] On 27 February 2022 the Council adopted resolution 2623 (2022), 11 in favour and one against (Russia), with three abstentions (China, India and the United Arab Emirates)."], [2, "[S1] It decided to call a General Assembly emergency special session on Ukraine, recording that permanent-member disagreement at its 8979th meeting had prevented the Council from exercising its primary responsibility."], [3, "[S3] Nebenzia, speaking for Russia, recorded a negative vote objecting to the draft recording the Council's inability to uphold its primary responsibility, distinguishing it from Russia's prior veto of draft S/2022/155."]], "source_excerpts": {"S0": "On 27 February 2022 the Security Council adopted resolution 2623 (2022) by 11 votes in favour, one against (Russia) and three abstentions (China, India and the United Arab Emirates). Russia's negative vote did not prevent adoption.", "S1": "The Council decided to call an emergency special session of the General Assembly to examine the Ukraine question on the agenda of its 8979th meeting. The resolution recorded that a lack of unanimity among permanent members at that earlier meeting had prevented the Council from exercising its primary responsibility.", "S2": "Brazil said it voted in favour despite reservations about the timing of the resolution and whether it would contribute to peace. It said urgency warranted adding the General Assembly's voice. Brazil stressed that the Council had yet to exhaust its instruments for supporting a negotiated and diplomatic solution.", "S3": "After presiding over the vote, Nebenzia explicitly spoke as Russia's representative. Russia explained its negative vote by objecting to the draft recording the Council's inability to uphold its primary responsibility. He distinguished this vote from Russia's veto of draft S/2022/155 at the earlier meeting."}}

{"candidate_paragraphs": [[1, "The Council adopted draft S/2022/980 as resolution 2669 (2022), by 12 votes in favour, none against and three abstentions. The United Kingdom voted in favour. China, India and Russia abstained. The resolution demands an immediate end to violence, calls for humanitarian access, and acknowledges ASEAN's central role. It requests the Secretary-General or his Special Envoy, in coordination with the ASEAN Special Envoy, to report orally to the Security Council by 15 March 2023."], [2, "United Kingdom — “The United Kingdom submitted the draft” “consultations with Council members, ASEAN members and regional partners” “It emphasized ending violence, humanitarian access and support for ASEAN efforts.”"], [3, "India as a delegation — “India praised the United Kingdom's consultation” “noted neighbouring countries' concerns” “advocated quiet, constructive diplomacy” “explained its abstention in light of those concerns.”"], [4, "Both delegations addressed regional concerns, while their votes differed."]], "criteria_in_order": ["Identify the adopted act as resolution 2669 (2022) and link it to draft S/2022/980.", "Give the 12–0–3 result and name the three abstentions.", "Identify the United Kingdom as sponsor and a yes vote. Give its supported rationale.", "Identify India's abstention and its preference for quiet, constructive diplomacy or its neighboring-country concerns.", "Separate the President's procedural announcement of adoption from India's national explanation of vote.", "Record the demands concerning ending violence and enabling humanitarian access.", "Preserve ASEAN's central role and coordination with the UN.", "Record shared attention to ASEAN or regional consultation while preserving the disagreement about the Council's action.", "Give the oral report to the Council, the 15 March 2023 deadline, the actor and ASEAN coordination.", "Keep the adopted resolution, the national positions and hypothetical workshop proposals distinct. A claim of unanimous adoption, Indian support, or a mandatory public aggregate report fails the fabrication guard."]}
